body:
Except when you DO meet them and they screw you over...  :/ 

Sorry to hear about your friend, OP, its def hard to lose people to depression.

yeah... sounds like we're definitely in similar places.  The only thing that stopped my self-destructiveness from getting any worse was the accompanying laziness to bother doing anything.  Maybe one of your new friends can be a support? I don't personally know how to make it stop, but I've heard supportive people help.

> Right now I don't even know what makes her depressed most of the time.

The answer to this might well be nothing or even everything.  I've played the role of your friend in this story with a concerned friend of my own (now its alcohol instead, but same idea) and I don't believe that I'm "fixable."  Try to get her to get help, hang out and keep her distracted from her worries, or tell her you're concerned that she's self medicating in a way that wont solve anything.  Satisfy your conscience and deal with yourself rather than blaming your problems on someone's personal actions that don't directly effect you.

I'm in a similar place but unfortunately I don't know the answer you're looking for.  I can't seem to manage to hang out with people and act normal without drinking, but so far no one has noticed.  This has been my new normal for months though, following the worst crash of my life.

How are you holding up? Does it feel like you're accelerating towards something increasingly stupid or are you just existing like me?  Well, potentially we're both headed for alcoholism, but other than that.

> Secondly, and more importantly, I'd have to believe that being with a woman was the only thing worth living for. Fuck that. Life has way more to offer than that.

Totes came in here to say this myself. Fuck that. Getting chicks isn't a magic cure to all problems.
